clue.text: Painter shows emperor and king together

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor
John was the King of England who sealed Magna Carta

explanation.surface: An artist puts an emperor and a king side by side in one exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus John was a Welsh portrait painter of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh artist famous for portraits, so he is an instance of a painter.

clue.text: One located in Canada, originally

indicators.note: something located in a place sits within it, so one letter is put inside the other piece
read as 'in an original way', telling us to rework the letters of Canada into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who lived in Canada in its earliest days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges CANADA into ACADAN, and 'located in' puts I inside it. Acadia was the early French colony in what is now Nova Scotia, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the first French settlement in maritime Canada, so its settlers were early inhabitants there.

clue.text: Flashy with new interior decoration

indicators.note: the new letter becomes the interior of the word for flashy, sitting inside it

parts.note: flashy means garish, gaudy

explanation.surface: Someone describes a showy piece of ornament with a fresh inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is an ornamental trimming added to food, a culinary decoration.

clue.text: Pass round wings of excellent goose

indicators.note: the mountain pass goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: the Simplon Pass is an Alpine route between Switzerland and Italy

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A goose with fine wings is passed round from hand to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings of' takes E and T, the first and last letters of 'excellent', and the Simplon Pass goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose is an informal word for a silly, foolish person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Shade one's lacking in part of Italy

indicators.note: the region's name is lacking the letter for one, so it is taken out

parts.note: Umbria is a region of central Italy
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Shade is said to be in short supply in a sunny Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbra is Latin for shadow and names the darkest central part of a cast shadow.

clue.text: Like a new arrival, given a girl's name

parts.note: someone who has only just come in has newly arrived

explanation.surface: A newborn baby girl is given her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Justina is a female forename, the feminine of Justin.

clue.text: Bird dog

definitions.meaning: a hawk that hunts low over open ground
a breed of hound used for hunting hares

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a bird of prey of the hawk family and to a breed of hare-hunting hound.

clue.text: Teacher resented being skilfully directed

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
to mind something is to object to or resent it

explanation.surface: A teacher grumbled about being steered cleverly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mastermind a scheme is to plan and run it cleverly, so the past tense means cleverly organised.

clue.text: A horse, followed by another animal, heads for shade, say

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A horse and then another beast make for the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' and 'shade' use the same five letters, so one is an example of a rearrangement of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another's letters is the term exemplified by this pair.

clue.text: Take Katherine's part? Damn

definitions.meaning: Katherine is the shrew of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, so playing her is being a shrew
an archaic curse meaning 'may evil befall'

explanation.definitionFit: An old curse word, which also splits as 'be shrew', acting the scold Shakespeare tamed.

clue.text: Having a reputation for being defiant

parts.note: with can mean having, as in a man with a hat
standing is one's status or reputation

explanation.surface: Someone is known for their rebellious streak.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to resist, so the participle describes holding out against opposition.

clue.text: Four or six in examination? It's not important

indicators.note: the number is placed in the word for examination, inside it

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination
IV is the Roman numeral for four; VI, for six, fits equally well

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether a score of four or six in a test matters at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Either IV or VI placed inside TRIAL gives the same answer, hence 'Four or six'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little significance or value.

clue.text: Believer taking a soulful view of things

definitions.text: Believer taking a soulful view of things

parts.words: Believer taking a soulful view of things
parts.note: describes one whose faith holds that objects, plants and places have souls, rather than a merely emotional person

explanation.definitionFit: Animism is the belief that natural objects possess spirits, so its follower credits things with souls.

clue.text: Drove 100 head of Hereford into farm

parts.note: to run cattle is to drive them
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drover took a hundred Hereford cattle into a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Herefords are a breed of beef cattle, so '100 head' reads as a herd count.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle.

clue.text: Ruth uses a new reference book

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Ruth turns to a fresh book to look something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a dictionary of synonyms, a book consulted for words.

clue.text: Order after which anything left should be disregarded?

definitions.text: Order after which anything left should be disregarded?

parts.words: Order after which anything left should be disregarded?
parts.note: a parade-ground command to turn the head to one side; 'left' means the other direction, not what remains

explanation.definitionFit: A drill command telling soldiers to turn their heads to the right.

clue.text: Wrongly enclose? In no respect

indicators.note: the letters of enclose are put together wrongly, in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an enclosure was done wrongly and is told it was not, not in any way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' rearranges ENCLOSE into SOLENCE, which follows IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, disrespectful behaviour, a lack of proper deference.

clue.text: Rescue inexperienced motorist in wild surroundings

indicators.note: the learner is in the middle of the word for wild
the word for wild forms surroundings for the learner letter

parts.note: savage means wild, untamed
L is the learner driver plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver stranded in rough country needs rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is saving property from loss, such as a ship or cargo from wreck.

clue.text: Tried to have political influence told stories about Bob's constituents

indicators.note: the word for told stories goes about the other letters, around them

parts.note: to tell stories can mean to lie

indicators.note: the letters constituting the name are taken and rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written without the possessive

explanation.surface: An MP fibbed to the voters in Bob's constituency to sway them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' rearranges BOB into OBB, which 'about' puts inside LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to try to sway legislators, so the past tense means pressed politicians.

clue.text: They support conductors and give backing to help opera

indicators.note: backing here means running in reverse, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
op. abbreviates opus, whose plural is opera

explanation.surface: Patrons sponsor an opera house to keep it going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give backing to' turns AID + OP round. A conductor stands on a podium; the plural here is the Latin form.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the raised platform an orchestral leader stands on, so these hold up maestros.

clue.text: Job available on island for worker given the sack

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is written on top of the next

parts.note: a post is a job or position open to be filled
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A job opening on an island goes to someone who has just been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the sack' suggests dismissal, but a postman carries a mail sack.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier is handed a bag of letters to deliver.

clue.text: Garment fitted in the middle

parts.note: the middle of the word fitted is a pair of Ts

explanation.surface: A tailor describes a jacket nipped in at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'fitted' shows a pair of Ts, read as a phrase naming that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Thinks about abolishing rate for French composer

indicators.note: the tax word is abolished, taken out of the longer word

parts.note: to deliberate is to think carefully about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician weighs up scrapping a local tax for the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Léo Delibes wrote the ballet Coppélia.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was a nineteenth-century French writer of ballet and opera music.

clue.text: Demonstrated fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who occupied a place sat in, and the same letters name a glossy silk cloth.

clue.text: Even pieces of gems are set in circular ring

indicators.note: jewels are set in a mounting, so these letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: round means circular

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of the word, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Gems are mounted in a round band to make a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even pieces of' takes E and S from 'gems', and 'are set in' puts them inside ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound is to echo or ring out loudly.

clue.text: Nobody was, for example, like Evelyn

definitions.text: Nobody was, for example, like Evelyn

parts.words: Nobody was, for example, like Evelyn
parts.note: Mr Pooter, the Nobody of the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, kept a journal, as did the seventeenth-century writer John Evelyn

explanation.definitionFit: A person who keeps a daily journal, like Pooter of The Diary of a Nobody or John Evelyn.

clue.text: Oriental musicians playing a melancholy piece

indicators.note: a piece of the phrase is taken, a run of letters spanning its words

explanation.surface: Eastern musicians are performing a sad tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like the musicians' activity, but it supplies the opening letter of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamelan is a traditional Indonesian ensemble of gongs and metallophones.

clue.text: Female's clear about new gregarious tendency

parts.note: her is the female possessive

indicators.note: the word for clear goes about the letter for new, around it

parts.note: distinct means clear, plain

explanation.surface: A woman is clear about a new sociable streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Herd instinct is the urge to follow the group, a sociable drive in animals and people.
